current_issues.problem: generated:ApplicableStructuralMemberShape is applied to every structural member, so members outside bottom structures and transverse side frames are rejected and are also forced to provide strength, collapse-load, and load-case data.

current_issues.problem: The candidate makes frameProfileType mandatory for every ship, although clause I2.6.1 contains no frame-profile-type requirement and the retrieved term is grounded in an unrelated TRAFICOM requirement.

current_issues.regression_guard: Do not impose frame-profile-type presence unless an applicable authoritative requirement explicitly requires it.

current_issues.problem: The candidate treats plasticStrength and midspanPlasticCollapseLoad as approximately equal using an undeclared tolerance and compares their signed values, while the requirement defines plastic strength by the magnitude of the midspan collapse load.
current_issues.required_change: Require plasticStrength to equal the magnitude of midspanPlasticCollapseLoad without the invented relative or absolute tolerance, unless an authoritative tolerance is supplied.
current_issues.regression_guard: Preserve the magnitude-based plastic-strength definition and do not introduce undeclared tolerances.

current_issues.problem: The comparison uses raw qudt:numericValue values for combinedShearAndBendingDemand and plasticStrength, but only plasticStrength is constrained to kN; demand has no unit compatibility or conversion constraint, so numerically comparing quantities expressed in different units can change conformance.
current_issues.required_change: Require the demand to use a unit compatible with the strength and convert both quantities to a common force unit before comparison, or constrain both operands to the same declared unit.
current_issues.regression_guard: Never compare quantity numeric values unless their units are identical or explicitly converted to a common compatible unit.
